mechanism_narrative: Persistent decline in TRANSIT mobility (-40 to -42 points over four weeks) signals sustained suppression of commuting and public movement. This structural reduction in transit access constrains retail foot traffic, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -36.7 to -42.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases relative to the baseline period despite TRANSIT remaining below -35 points in all four weeks of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating RETAIL_REC decline (from -14.0 to -19.1 over four weeks) reflects cumulative consumer avoidance behavior. This trend continuation signal predicts RETAIL_REC will remain depressed or decline further over the next four weeks as behavioral caution persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined 5.1 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the prior 28 days by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapsed from -4.6 to -20.0 points over four weeks, indicating suppression of outdoor recreation. When outdoor alternatives contract sharply, consumers shift demand toward indoor retail venues, producing a rebound in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -4.6 to -20.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below -15 points in all four weeks of the forecast period despite PARKS being suppressed below -15 points.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility (declining only -1.6 to -5.9 points) combined with accelerating RETAIL_REC decline indicates consumers are prioritizing essential purchases while avoiding discretionary retail. This bifurcation will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed relative to the prior period.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM decline is less than half the magnitude of RETAIL_REC decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM converge to within 3 percentage points of each other during the forecast period, indicating resumed discretionary spending.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains suppressed at -15 to -16 points across all four weeks, signaling continued remote work or workplace restrictions. Sustained workplace suppression prevents the return of commute-linked retail spending, constraining RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains between -15 and -17 points for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES ranged from -15.7 to -16.3 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next four weeks while WORKPLACES remains below -14 points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility elevated at +8.1 to +8.7 points across all four weeks indicates sustained home confinement. High residential occupancy combined with depressed TRANSIT (-40 to -42) creates a regime where consumers lack mobility to reach retail venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC further.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +8 points AND TRANSIT remains below -40 points simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases despite the simultaneous presence of elevated RESIDENTIAL and depressed TRANSIT throughout the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-August timing (decision date 2020-08-15) marks the end of summer peak season. Seasonal demand contraction combined with observed RETAIL_REC decline trend will accelerate as back-to-school and fall transitions reduce discretionary retail traffic over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: calendar date is mid-August to mid-September
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points during the four-week forecast period despite seasonal headwinds.

mechanism_narrative: Divergence between GROCERY_PHARM stability (-5.9) and RETAIL_REC deterioration (-19.1) at t-0w, combined with PARKS collapse (-20.0), signals a regime shift toward essential-only mobility. This behavioral lock-in will prevent RETAIL_REC recovery as consumers maintain avoidance of discretionary venues over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC is more than 13 points below GROCERY_PHARM AND PARKS is below -15 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC gap to GROCERY_PHARM narrows to less than 8 percentage points within two weeks, indicating resumption of discretionary spending.
